newsitem.title: USA: Crop boosting rain forecast for south Midwest--WSC.
newsitem.headline: Crop boosting rain forecast for south Midwest--WSC.

text.p: Corn and soybean crops in the southern Midwest should receive favorable rains later Tuesday and early Wednesday, said Mike Palmerino, senior agricultural meteorologist for Weather Services Corp.

He noted the bulk of the rain from a system currently moving across Kansas and Missouri would fall south of a line from Dayton, Ohio to St. Louis, Missouri. Palmerino said heavy weekend showers were concentrated north of that line.
"I think it is a very beneficial rain event for soybeans in those areas," WSC's Palmerino said. Rainfall was seen totalling 0.30 to 1.00 inch.
Temperatures in the U.S. Midwest, which are already below normal, were seen falling further later in the week.
"You are already rather cool (in the U.S. Midwest) and there is going to be some reinforcing cool air as we head on into the second half of the week," Palmerino said.

He noted temperatures were currently a few degrees below normal with highs around 75 to 80 degrees Fahrenheit versus a normal 80 to 82 degrees. From Thursday into the weekend highs were seen dropping down to around 70 to 75 degrees.
"I think the real concern is that it will lead towards slower development and maturation of corn and to a lesser extent soybeans," Palmerino said.
He said delayed development could make corn vulnerable if there was an early freeze in mid-September, adding that chances of a freeze in the next three weeks is, however, an "extreme long shot."
